newsitem.title: USA: Aasche sees Southwest Division Q2 profit.
newsitem.headline: Aasche sees Southwest Division Q2 profit.

text.p: Aasche Transportation Services Inc said Wednesday it expects its Southwest Division will return to profitability in the second quarter.
After losing $97,000 during January and February, the Southwest Division was nearly break-even in March, the company said.

"We believe that the Southwest Division should return to profitability during the second quarter," Larry Asche, chairman, said in a statement. "Our plan to address the driver shortage problems, operating inefficiencies, asset utilization concerns, and equipment debt issues of the Southwest Division was a difficult one, but appears to be successful."
Earlier, Aasche Transportation reported first quarter net income of $0.02 a share, even with $0.02 a year ago after a $0.02 charge.

Aasche Transportation provides temperature-controlled, time-sensitive transportation of frozen foods, juice concentrates, perishable commodities, household and retail commodities, and tropical foliage.
